source_timestamp: Ministry of Transport list of 2025-07-31 (cumulative 1 to 31 July 2025, as published by The Bangkok Insight); OpenStreetMap extract retrieved 2026-07-10T02:46:49Z; COD-AB boundaries valid on 2022-01-22
confidence_basis: Positions from OpenStreetMap ways, milestones and COD-AB tambons, none checked on the ground; one of the four routes is not in OSM and one is placed only to a 29 km stretch.
assumptions: OpenStreetMap is the Geofabrik extract recorded in outputs/open_context_data_file_manifest.csv (retrieved 2026-07-10), a year after the event; a road, milestone or hospital mapped differently in July 2025 is not seen.

A milestone's distance tag is the official km of the route at that node; between two milestones the official km is spread evenly along the merged OSM line, and beyond the last one the line is read at one OSM metre per official metre.
A milestone counts as on the route when it lies within 30 m of the merged route line; it is moved onto the line.

Tambon names of the list are matched to COD-AB tha_admin3 polygons (boundaries valid 2022-01-22); the COD-AB polygons and the OSM roads were not drawn together and can disagree by a few hundred metres.
A route of the list is found only by its reference on OSM ways (or a name that carries the route number); a road not tagged that way is recorded as not found and given no position.
Hospitals are OSM map records; their operation, entrances and the parts that flooded are not checked here.
what_this_is: The positions of the reported road cuts and of the two hospitals of the Nan case, placed before any flag of the frame is computed (test 3b and test 4 of the protocol). Positions only: nothing here is set against radar, a flood map or a reference layer.
attribution: Road, milestone and hospital positions © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database Licence 1.0 (ODbL); tambon boundaries: HDX Thailand COD-AB (OCHA, RTSD).

rules.placement: Protocol test 3b: each point placed on the OpenStreetMap way with that route reference, by milestone nodes where they exist, otherwise as the part of the route inside the named tambon.
rules.milestones: highway=milestone nodes whose ref names the route and whose distance tag gives a km, within 30 m of the merged route line, moved onto it. Two or more: the official km is interpolated linearly between the bracketing milestones and read at one OSM metre per official metre beyond the first or last. One milestone at km 0 within 100 m of a route end: one OSM metre per official metre from it.
rules.route_line: The OSM ways that carry the route reference, merged; the longest merged line is the route line. A rural road's bare number counts only on ways that touch Nan province.
rules.not_found: A route with no OSM way carrying its reference is recorded as not found and gets no position.
rules.se2_routing_geometry: the union of the 35 frame units buffered by 3000 m in EPSG:32647 (16 segments per quarter circle)

hospitals.identification: Identified as OSM way 315323384: tagged amenity=hospital, name:th โรงพยาบาลน่าน, the address 1 Worawichai, emergency=yes, operator Ministry of Public Health and Wikidata Q18118091, whose coordinates (about 18.795 N, 100.789 E) fall on the site. summary.note: Test 3b counts the share of the four listed points found; a point with no position cannot be found, and the test stage must say how it is counted.
notes_for_the_test_stage: Highway 1243 km 59+100 is placed by the protocol's tambon rule as the whole stretch of the route in Nam Muap (about 29.5 km), so its 300 m buffer takes in every edge of that stretch. Report only: reading the OSM line from its southern end puts km 59+100 in Nam Muap and the only bridge of the route inside Nam Muap (way 314512631) at km 58.49 to 58.52, 0.36 km from the washed-out bridge approach of the 1 August list (km 58+875 to 58+900).

Nan 4020 km 10+500 to 10+900 is placed by milestones in Kong Khwai (Mueang Nan), about 0.5 km beyond the road's stretch in Na Pang, which the list names; within 300 m of the placed part lies part of the unit-scale reading, not the Na Pang stretch.
Nan 021 has no position. The Department of Rural Roads list of 26 July 2025 gives it, both stretches of Nan 4020 and Nan 3019 as impassable that day.

order_rule: Written before any flag of the Nan frame is computed and before the freeze; the stage refuses to re-place after the freeze. The coordinator commits this file before the test stage runs.
firewall: This lane opened no radar, flood map or reference layer: not the sealed JAXA folder, not any GFM file, not the THEOS-2 files of 31 July 2025 nor anything derived from them. Every path was checked against that list before it was opened.
limits: Positions are OpenStreetMap data, not surveyed; the km of a cut comes from the list, its place on the map from the milestones or the tambon.
The list is a month's cumulative summary: it says where roads were affected during 1 to 31 July 2025, not when each cut began or ended.
Nothing here is a flag or a flood map; the points are placed before any flag of the frame is computed.
Planning guidance only; not an official warning.
